title: Three-statement forecasting
review_type: Independent specialist full-manuscript, prompt-solution, method, primary-source and computation audit
recommendation: Ready for coordinator acceptance after v07-c09 and shared integration gates.
method_review: Forecast/scenario/budget distinction and quantity-price interaction taught before problems. Case units are kCU, thousands of units and CU unit prices; original illustrative annual periods are not observed data.

Opening balances, wholly credit sales/purchases, AR/inventory/AP rollforwards, purchase-based AP target, expense-payment timing, year-end service convention and book/tax equality consistently applied.

Old assets and new year-end capex are separate depreciation cohorts. Opening debt determines main-case interest; final-date revolver changes therefore do not cause current interest. Endogenous next-year interest correctly carries forward.

Cash minimum, total revolver limit, zero-debt lower bound and retained excess cash are explicitly distinguished. A failed funding year is not represented as a feasible balance sheet or followed by an unsupported later forecast.

Average-debt example is a separate contract. Algebra has funding slope1-k>0; positive, zero-debt and binding-limit branches checked. Full current tax relief is an assumption tested against positive profit in manuscript examples, not established by the helper.

Cash gap and gross debt gap differ under average interest; intrayear availability and annual ending cash remain separate constraints. Financing access and operating capacity are not certified by arithmetic.

All eight solutions answer exact prompts; open reasoning asks for concrete evidence or operational premises. Teach-back and capex-retention answers propagate tax, interest, depreciation and capital consistently.

Exercise7 correctly demonstrates that A=L+E can survive contradictory cash paths. The wrong immediate-expensing tax assumption is explicitly identified and the correct schedule restored; a fictional equity plug is rejected.

Visual/mobile/print UI QA and whole-library integration remain coordinator tasks.
